scene: Violent deaths, last-minute repentance and the memory of Jacopo, Buonconte and Pia
story: Dante's living body blocks the light and casts a shadow. Passing souls notice, call out, and turn toward the travelers. Virgil tells Dante not to stop merely because others are talking about him.
A company of souls who died violently approaches, singing the Miserere. They beg Dante, who is alive, to carry their names to the living so that prayers may help them.
Jacopo del Cassero recalls fleeing assassins near Oriago and bleeding to death in the marsh. He asks Dante to arrange prayers in Fano.

Buonconte da Montefeltro recounts his death after the battle of Campaldino. At his last breath, he invokes Mary, and an angel takes his soul, while a demon raises a storm that sweeps his body away. This is Buonconte's account within the poem.
Pia de' Tolomei speaks briefly: Siena made her, Maremma undid her. She asks to be remembered, alluding to her husband and the ring of marriage without spelling out every circumstance of her death.
The travelers continue up the mountain carrying the names and petitions of those who cannot themselves return to the living.

semanticSomatic.semantic: A living witness can carry testimony across the boundary between the dead and living

alchemicalReading: Three forms of last-moment conversion: remembrance carries the account; prayer gives it a destination; brevity preserves what is unknown.
invariant: A testimony can be carried faithfully without converting reported events into first-hand observation or filling gaps with conjecture.
